category_title: Less-verbal students with HFA who struggle with contextual shifts and social pressure
student_description: K is a technically patient student who struggles significantly with social complexity, contextual shifts, and imaginative play. He becomes overwhelmed and passive when facing simultaneous interactions or group demands. To thrive, he uniquely requires carefully scaffolded imaginative prompts, 1-on-1 peer pairing rather than groups, and a structured balance between forced collaboration (via resource limits) and private, individualized spaces.

criteria.rationale: Because K takes imaginative prompts literally and shuts down if they are too complex, he needs step-by-step introduction to role-play.
criteria.check: The tutor introduces imaginative or social design elements gradually, breaking down role-play requests into smaller, manageable steps rather than demanding immediate, complex acting.

criteria.rationale: K becomes overwhelmed and passive when forced to process multiple social inputs or partner requests at the exact same time.
criteria.check: The tutor limits the immediate interaction to a single social or design demand at a time, avoiding forcing K to respond to multiple peers or complex contextual shifts simultaneously.
